evals.name: daily-full-sweep
evals.prompt: hey can you run the daily competitor check for AgentScore - see what's new with langfuse, arize, patronus, all of them, and write it up
evals.expected_output: A new dated markdown file at docs/research/competitive-intel/YYYY-MM-DD.md, with a section per competitor pulled from docs/research/competitive-analysis-report.md, each with dated/sourced bullets across the three buckets (update, customers love, using it for) where findings exist, empty-handed competitors omitted, and a short final report summarizing counts.
assertions: Competitor list was read from docs/research/competitive-analysis-report.md rather than invented/hardcoded
Each finding has a real, working source link
"Customers love" bullets name a specific feature/workflow, not generic praise (e.g. not just "great tool")
"Using it for" bullets describe concrete usage/integration, distinct in substance from the "love" bullets
A competitor with nothing new is omitted entirely rather than given an empty/placeholder section
First-run dedup handling is correct: no prior digest exists, so nothing is wrongly filtered out as a duplicate
"So what for AgentScore" synthesis is present only if something materially matters, not forced every time
Final report states counts (competitors with findings vs. skipped) and the output file path

evals.name: single-competitor-focus
evals.prompt: what's new with Patronus AI specifically? anything customers are raving about lately
evals.expected_output: Focuses research on Patronus AI (still checks/writes the dated digest file per the skill's normal workflow, or at minimum surfaces the three-bucket findings for Patronus AI specifically), with sourced, specific claims rather than generic praise.
assertions: Research stays scoped to Patronus AI rather than sweeping unrelated competitors
Findings are specific and sourced, not generic sentiment
Handles the single-competitor scope sensibly (doesn't force the full multi-competitor digest workflow onto a one-company ask, or if it does, does so in a way that still reads naturally)
Distinguishes 'customers love' (sentiment) from 'using it for' (behavior) rather than collapsing them into one bucket
